summary: Attacked part 2 of the Curves, abelian varieties and Shimura varieties area — AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty, ArithmeticDynamics, EffectiveDiophantineMethods, FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems, HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions, InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups and NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties: 7 roadmaps, 47 stages, 65 accepted paper routes, 30 of them into one 7-stage roadmap. Two findings, both medium and both objects that no layer in the atlas names: the pro-etale fundamental group of Bhatt-Scholze, which a routed paper needs and which IG.0's profinite construction is not, and the assertion about finitely generated closed normal subgroups of absolute Galois groups, whose route is recorded UNACCEPTED and asks for an ownership decision. Bookkeeping and the library boundary are clean, and one lead dissolved because another red team had already examined it correctly.
checked: All 47 stages of the seven roadmaps with their descriptions, dependencies and acceptance clauses, and the accepted audit verdict for each: 44 not built, 3 partly built, 3 process.

Eligibility, measured rather than assumed: none of the papers this session has reviewed routes into this part, checked at route granularity across all 207 paper result files. Unlike part 1, where PAPER-VANHOFTEN-24 required a disclosure, there is no entanglement here.

All 65 routes and their reasons in full. The distribution is very uneven: InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups takes 30 across its 7 stages (IG.0 10, IG.1 9, IG.2 6, IG.4 5, IG.3 4), HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions 15 (RP.0 6, RP.2 6), FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems 6 (R28.4 6), NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties 6, AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty 4, ArithmeticDynamics 2, EffectiveDiophantineMethods 2.

Dependency bookkeeping, the head that produced a finding in part 1 of the Algebraic number theory area. Clean: for every one of the seven roadmaps the set of roadmaps reached by a cross-roadmap stage `requires` edge is contained in its declared `prerequisites`, so no stage edge is unrecorded. Declared prerequisite counts run from 3 to 7 and consumer counts from 1 to 9, so no roadmap here has the empty-consumers shape that needed a sink check in the Analytic and part-1 areas.

A systematic scan of all 65 route reasons for the highest-signal pattern, a route that records its own unmet need — UNACCEPTED, 'does not name', 'does not own', 'no owner', 'ownership decision', 'needs a separate', 'not supplied by'. Three matched. One is the second finding below. The other two are ordinary ownership disclaimers that defer to an owner which exists: PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18's note that 'LD.6 consumes this interface and does not own a second ordinary height construction', and PAPER-BRESCIANI-24's note about a generic theorem its own route does not own.

That BRESCIANI-24 lead, which dissolved, and how. Its route says the geometric application 'imports the generic split-completion theorem from the proposed ProfiniteProPGroups Part II; this source route does not own that generic theorem', and no such roadmap exists in either directory — 'split-completion' returns 0 files across all roadmap records. That reads as a dependency on something absent. It is not: the paper extraction itself proposes a new roadmap, ProfiniteProPGroupsPartIISplitCompletion with 7 items, which is the programme's mechanism for exactly this, and RT-AREA-grouptheory has already examined that proposal and recorded in its `checked` list that its title 'is an exact prefix extension of the parent's atlas title'. So the need is both raised and already reviewed by another red team, and filing it here would duplicate accepted work.

Whether the pro-etale fundamental group of the first finding is owned under another name, before calling it absent. 'pro-etale fundamental', 'proetale fundamental' and their accented forms return 0 files across both roadmap directories, as do 'geometrically unibranch' and 'infinite Galois category', which are the hypotheses and the framework that statement needs. 'pro-etale' itself returns 18 files, but those are the pro-etale topology and site in the adic, prismatic and ring-stack roadmaps, not the fundamental group. Bhatt-Scholze is cited in 6 roadmaps, and the only citation of the pro-etale topology paper in a relevant context is EnhancedDerivedSheaves, which cites it for replete-topos results — 'Prove the replete-topos results used from Bhatt-Scholze, The pro-etale topology for schemes, section 3: the needed exactness of inverse limits of surjections, convergence of derived Postnikov towers, and unbounded cohomological descent'. That is section 3 of the paper, not the fundamental group of its later sections.

Whether the absolute-Galois statement of the second finding is owned, likewise checked under other descriptions. 'closed normal subgroup' returns 4 files and none is it: ProfiniteProPGroups uses it for quotients of profinite groups and for the closed normal subgroup generated by a relator, BelyiMaps for topologically characteristic subgroups and continuous outer automorphisms, ArithmeticGaloisDuality for the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence of a closed normal subgroup, and MordellLawrenceVenkatesh for closed normal subgroups of SL_2 and of products of symplectic groups. None concerns finitely generated closed normal subgroups of an absolute Galois group.

The library boundary, which as in part 1 can yield little and for the same reason: 44 of the 47 stages are audited `not built`, including all seven of EffectiveDiophantineMethods, all six of FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems and all six of NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties. The only stages that are not `not built` are two partly-built ArithmeticDynamics stages, one partly-built InverseGalois stage, and three `process` stages. There is almost nothing in the libraries for these stages to duplicate.

A cross-area observation worth recording for the programme rather than as a finding of its own. PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16 now has two UNACCEPTED routes in two different areas, each blocked for want of an owner: this area's IG.2 route below, and its AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4 route, which RT-AREA-analytic filed as a finding because the arithmetic-scheme form of Chebotarev density has no owner. One paper generating two ownership gaps in different areas suggests its remaining unrouted content is worth a deliberate ownership pass rather than route-by-route triage.

Library trees, with sizes printed beside every result after two wrong paths produced false cleans earlier in this session: a full Mathlib checkout of 8556 .lean files and the Tau Ceti library tree of 5268.

findings.where: InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0 (Galois categories and fibre functors), and the atlas as a whole
findings.claim: The pro-etale fundamental group has no owner. IG.0 constructs the profinite automorphism group of the geometric fibre functor on finite etale covers, and that is a different object: the pro-etale fundamental group of Bhatt-Scholze classifies locally constant sheaves rather than finite covers, is prodiscrete rather than profinite, and needs its own hypotheses on the scheme. PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17 routes to IG.0 and its route says in so many words that it 'widens' the stage to that object, naming the equivalence it needs. No layer in either roadmap directory names the pro-etale fundamental group, and the one roadmap that cites the Bhatt-Scholze paper cites a different part of it for a different purpose.
findings.evidence: IG.0's construction clause reads: 'Construct the profinite automorphism group of the geometric fibre functor on finite etale covers, together with its equivalence to finite continuous sets. Treat connected components and base-point change as explicit equivalences', with acceptance 'Recover the absolute Galois group for Spec K and the fundamental group of G_m over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field'. PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17's route to IG.0 quotes that clause and then states the gap: 'This route widens it to the pro-etale fundamental group of Bhatt-Scholze for connected, locally topologically noetherian schemes, with the equivalence between J_b(Q_p)-torsors on S_proet and continuous homomorphisms pi_1^proet(S, xbar) -> J_b(Q_p), used in Proposition 1.13 and Remark 4.3.14.' Ownership searches across research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/ and research/blueprint/roadmaps/: 'pro-etale fundamental', 'proetale fundamental' and the accented forms return 0 files; 'geometrically unibranch' and 'infinite Galois category', the hypothesis and the framework the construction requires, return 0; 'pro-etale' returns 18 files but every one is the pro-etale topology or site in adic, prismatic and ring-stack roadmaps. Bhatt-Scholze is cited by 6 roadmaps, and the only citation of The pro-etale topology for schemes in a related context is EnhancedDerivedSheaves, for section 3's replete-topos results — 'the needed exactness of inverse limits of surjections, convergence of derived Postnikov towers, and unbounded cohomological descent' — which is neither the fundamental group nor its torsor equivalence.
findings.fix: Give the pro-etale fundamental group a named owner. The economical choice is a stage in this roadmap after IG.0, since IG.0 already owns Galois categories, fibre functors and base-point change and the pro-etale theory is their extension: state the pro-etale site of a connected, locally topologically noetherian scheme, the prodiscrete fundamental group pi_1^proet(S, xbar) as automorphisms of the fibre functor on locally constant sheaves, the comparison map from it to the finite-etale pi_1 of IG.0, and the equivalence between G(Q_p)-torsors on S_proet and continuous homomorphisms pi_1^proet(S, xbar) -> G(Q_p) that PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17 consumes. Bhatt-Scholze, The pro-etale topology for schemes, is the source, and its section 3 replete-topos results are already owned by EnhancedDerivedSheaves, which should be recorded as the supplier rather than duplicated. If the material is judged to belong with the adic and pro-etale-site roadmaps instead, the fix is to say which one owns it, because at present a route points at a stage that constructs a different group.

findings.where: InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.2 (Hilbert irreducibility), and the atlas as a whole
findings.claim: The statement about finitely generated closed normal subgroups of absolute Galois groups has no owner, and the atlas already records that it does not: PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16's route to IG.2 is marked UNACCEPTED and asks for an ownership decision. IG.2 owns ordinary Hilbert irreducibility, which is strictly weaker, and the route says so. Nothing in either roadmap directory owns the stronger assertion under any description I could find, so an accepted extraction has a route that cannot be accepted, and the blocking reason is an absent owner rather than a defect in the paper.
findings.evidence: The route, PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16 to InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.2, in full: 'UNACCEPTED candidate: IG.2 owns ordinary Hilbert irreducibility. The substantially stronger assertion about finitely generated closed normal subgroups of absolute Galois groups needs a source-level derivation, its exact field hypotheses and an ownership decision. The checked number-field argument uses FJ08 16.11.6 and Weissauer's theorem; another extraction's planned tag does not establish this contract (G2).' The last clause matters: a second extraction has already tagged this as planned and this one records that the tag does not establish the contract, so the gap has been noticed twice from opposite directions. Ownership search: 'closed normal subgroup' returns 4 files across both roadmap directories and none is this statement — tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGroups uses the phrase for quotients of a profinite group by a closed normal subgroup and for the closed normal subgroup generated by a relator, tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/BelyiMaps for topologically characteristic closed normal subgroups and continuous outer automorphisms, ArithmeticGaloisDuality for the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence of a closed normal subgroup, and MordellLawrenceVenkatesh for closed normal subgroups of SL_2 and of products of symplectic groups.
findings.fix: Make the ownership decision the route asks for. The statement is about absolute Galois groups rather than about Hilbert sets, so IG.2 is the wrong home as scoped and a new stage or a Part II layer should own it: the assertion for finitely generated closed normal subgroups of the absolute Galois group of a field, with the exact field hypotheses stated rather than inherited, and Fried-Jarden 16.11.6 together with Weissauer's theorem as the sources the route names. Whoever makes the decision should also reconcile the other extraction's planned tag, which this route says does not establish the contract, so that the two records agree. Once an owner exists the route can be accepted; until then it should stay UNACCEPTED rather than be absorbed into IG.2, because Hilbert irreducibility does not imply it.
